_comment: Canonical node-key filename fixture (F-08), specified in HUP_SPEC.md §4.1.
so the two SDKs cannot name the same node's key file differently again.
The algorithm, restated from HUP_SPEC.md §4.1 step 5:
1. sanitised = node_id with every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._:-]
replaced by '_'. The class is exactly the brain's NodeRegisterPayload
node_id pattern, and it is ASCII: 'é' is not a member even though
Python's str.isalnum() says it is a letter.
2. If sanitised == node_id and 1 <= len(node_id) <= 128, the filename is
sanitised + '.key'. Every node id the brain accepts takes this branch,
so no already-paired node changes filename.
makes step 1 injective again: replacement alone maps both 'a b' and
Every 'before' pair below was measured on the pre-fix source.

cases.name: plain
cases.why: already legal; both SDKs agreed and the filename must not move

cases.name: colons
cases.why: ':' is in the allowed class; unchanged

cases.name: all_allowed_punctuation
cases.why: the full punctuation set survives untouched

cases.name: space
cases.why: the audit's headline case: a node paired through one SDK re-paired under the other

cases.name: underscore_lookalike
cases.why: must NOT collide with 'sensor 01'. Under the old TS rule it did: both were sensor_01.key

cases.name: non_ascii_letter
cases.why: Python's str.isalnum() is Unicode-aware and kept 'é'; the TS class is ASCII and dropped it

cases.name: space_collision_a
cases.why: pairs with space_collision_b to prove the mapping is injective

cases.name: space_collision_b
cases.why: the old TS rule mapped this and 'a b' onto one file; the old Python rule mapped 'a b' onto 'ab.key' instead

cases.name: all_punctuation
cases.why: Python dropped every character and wrote a hidden file literally named '.key', which EVERY all-punctuation node id shared

cases.name: empty
cases.why: both SDKs wrote the same hidden '.key' file as the all-punctuation case above

cases.name: cjk
cases.why: the TS form collided with every other 6-character non-ASCII node id

cases.name: emoji
cases.why: astral plane, and a SECOND independent divergence the audit does not name: the TS regex had no 'u' flag, so it matched per UTF-16 unit and made a surrogate pair two underscores, where Python's re matches per code point and makes one

cases.name: traversal_attempt
cases.why: '/' is outside the allowed class in both rules, so neither SDK ever escaped the keys directory. Pinned so that stays true.

cases.name: max_length
cases.why: 128 characters is the brain's ceiling and still takes the unchanged branch

cases.name: over_max_length
cases.why: 129 characters is truncated and hashed, so an over-long id can never produce a filename the filesystem refuses
